name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on some rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing stays in force
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of export controls on five rare earths and related processing technology, due to end on 10 Nov, to 10 Jan 2027, with curbs on some lithium battery and graphite materials also still paused (S&P Global). Licensing controls imposed in April 2025 on seven rare earths, including dysprosium and terbium, remain in force, so Watch holds. Searches on 16 Nov found no production stoppages outside China linked to export bans.
for_you: Makers of electric vehicles, wind turbines, electronics and defence equipment that rely on Chinese rare earths remain exposed to licensing delays and price swings.
rubric_hit: Watch: April 2025 rare-earth licensing controls still in force; no ban-linked stoppages outside China

sources.title: S&P Global — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
